contracts.blurb: Neighbourhood shops want yaji sachets and kilishi by the till.
A Lagos chain gives Musa's spice jars a full snack shelf.
Hotels and party caterers order marinated grill packs in bulk.
Distributors truck boxed kilishi to motor parks in other states.
ECOWAS buyers take pallets of kilishi and yaji across the border.
Diaspora shops in Peckham and Houston can't keep it on the shelf.

belt.name: Skewer Conveyor Grill
belt.blurb: Sticks ride over the coals and arrive at the counter hot.

auto.name: Cold Room Meat Slicer
auto.blurb: Slices and skewers beef, chicken and goat without a farmhand.

pack.name: Vacuum Seal Line
pack.blurb: Seals kilishi and yaji airtight so they survive the trip abroad.

milestones.title: Second Fire Lit
milestones.blurb: Your first suya spot outside the flagship. The same yaji must taste the same there.

milestones.title: Five Grills in Lagos
milestones.blurb: Island and Mainland both covered. You now buy beef by the half cow, not by the kilo.

milestones.title: Central Spice Kitchen
milestones.blurb: One kitchen blends yaji for every spot, so your secret recipe stays secret.

milestones.title: Suya Reaches Abuja
milestones.blurb: Spots open in Abuja, Ibadan and Port Harcourt. Refrigerated trucks join the fleet.

milestones.title: Own Cattle Ranch Deal
milestones.blurb: You sign ranchers in the north directly. Meat costs drop and quality stays steady.

milestones.title: A Spot in Every State
milestones.blurb: From Sokoto to Calabar, travellers plan their road stops around your grills.

milestones.title: West Africa Smoke
milestones.blurb: Accra, Cotonou and Dakar queue for suya. Your kilishi is the region's road snack.

milestones.title: Peckham Grand Opening
milestones.blurb: The first London spot sells out by 9 PM. Diaspora customers bring their neighbours.

milestones.title: Houston to Toronto
milestones.blurb: North America falls for asun and masa. Airport kiosks sell kilishi as gifts.

milestones.title: Suya Capital of the World
milestones.blurb: 500 spots on four continents, and it all started with one grill and one newspaper.

staff: Fire dey hot, suya dey ready!
Who order chicken with extra yaji?
Abeg bring more onions and tomato.
Charcoal don finish, I dey go store.
Turn that stick before e burn o!
Asun for table six, e dey come!
Masa just comot fire, soft like pillow.
My hand don sabi this knife.
Wrap am for paper, add toothpick.
Smoke dey my eye but money dey come.
One more tray of beef for grill!
Queue long reach road, make we hurry.
customer: Abeg add plenty pepper for me.
This asun dey scatter my head!
Chicken suya, cut am small small.
I fit get masa to follow am?
Zobo first, pepper don catch me.
Na this aroma bring me from Lekki.
Put extra onions, no be fight.
My wife say make I no come empty.
Best suya for Lagos, no argument.
Pack kilishi, I dey travel tomorrow.
Is the goat meat fresh today?
Ah, this yaji get secret inside.
One more stick, last one, I promise.
manager: Oga, all the grills dey full today.
Wash hand before you touch meat!
Meat truck go land by 7 AM sharp.
Smile for customer, e dey add tip.
Yaji stock low, I don order more.
Export truck dey wait for bay, sir.
Nobody chop suya on duty, abeg.
Sales pass yesterday own, well done!
night: My cloth still dey smell of smoke.
Tomorrow I go buy bigger grill.
From one stick to all this. Wow.
Even my dream get suya aroma.
Mama go proud of this spot.
Sleep now, fire must light by 8.

events.name: Friday Night Suya Rush
events.text: Offices close early and everybody wants suya for the weekend.

events.name: Heavy Evening Rain
events.text: Rain chases the crowd indoors and the open grill stays quiet.

events.name: Big Match Night
events.text: Football fans pay extra for hot suya before kick-off.

events.name: Cattle Truck Delayed
events.text: The meat truck from the north is stuck on the expressway.

events.name: Charcoal Price Jump
events.text: Charcoal sellers raise prices and today's fire costs more.

events.name: Wedding Party Order
events.text: A caterer pays cash upfront for 300 sticks and a tray of asun.

events.name: Food Blogger Visit
events.text: A famous food blogger films your grill and big spenders follow.

events.name: Harmattan Breeze
events.text: Dry wind keeps the coals glowing and the meat cooks faster.

research.claim: A Lagos suya-focused quick-service chain opened its 12th location, in Yaba, in December 2024, showing suya scales as a multi-branch restaurant brand.
The same suya chain is reported to have grown from N20,000 of starting capital to about N5 billion despite rising costs.
Nigerian kilishi producers are packaging the dried spiced meat for international markets and global retail shelves.
Nigerian suya restaurants operate in diaspora hubs in Texas, such as a suya spot in Euless near Fort Worth.
